members.summary: Predicts, for each token, how much each LoRA expert should weigh.
members.extended:
A stack of `xlora_depth` linear layers (ReLU and dropout between them) over the hidden
states, `(batch, tokens, hidden_size)` to `(batch, tokens, n_classes)` — or
`n_classes * n_layers` outputs with `layerwise_scalings`, spread over the adapted layers.
The result is `(batch, tokens, n_layers, n_classes)`, softmax-normalised over the experts
(at `softmax_temperature`) unless `enable_softmax` is off.  It reads its settings from
the config it is given, so changing the config's `softmax_temperature` or
`scaling_pass_value` takes effect at the next call.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The classifier's shape (`hidden_size` set) and behaviour.

parameters.name: n_classes
parameters.description: How many experts it weighs.

parameters.name: n_layers
parameters.description: How many adapted layers the weights are for.

parameters.name: dtype
parameters.description:
The dtype of its parameters and of the weights it returns (the adapter's: the base
model's, float32 for a half-precision one).

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: The device it lives on (the base model's).

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.peft import XLoraConfig
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.xlora._classifier import XLoraClassifier
>>> config = XLoraConfig(hidden_size=8, adapters={"a": "x", "b": "y"})
>>> classifier = XLoraClassifier(config, n_classes=2, n_layers=3, dtype=lucid.float32, device="cpu")
>>> classifier(lucid.randn(1, 5, 8)).shape
(1, 5, 3, 2)

members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` mixes LoRA adapters with X-LoRA.
members.extended:
X-LoRA (Buehler & Buehler, 2024, [arXiv:2402.07148](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07148)) keeps several trained LoRA adapters (the
experts) and a small classifier on the base model's final hidden states that scales each
expert per token: a scalings pass computes the hidden states with the experts held at a
fixed value, the classifier turns them into one weight per expert (per adapted layer if
`layerwise_scalings`), and the real pass adds each expert's update with its weight.  Only the
classifier trains unless `use_trainable_adapters`.

Field names, their order, defaults and `adapter_config.json` are the reference adapter library's.  Unlike the reference's, `hidden_size` left unset is read off the model
rather than guessed, and an empty `adapters` is refused when the model is built.

parameters.description:
The experts: each name maps to the directory of a saved LoRA adapter.  They are loaded
under the names `"0"`, `"1"`, ... in this order, which is also the order of the
classifier's outputs.  Needed when the model is built.

parameters.name: enable_softmax
parameters.description: Normalise each token's expert weights with a softmax.

parameters.name: enable_softmax_topk
parameters.description: Softmax over the `top_k_lora` kept experts instead; set `enable_softmax` off with it.

parameters.name: layerwise_scalings
parameters.description:
One set of weights per adapted layer (the classifier outputs `n_experts * n_layers`)
instead of one set shared by every layer.

parameters.name: xlora_depth
parameters.description: Linear layers of the classifier.

parameters.name: xlora_size
parameters.description: Width of its hidden layers; unused at depth one.

parameters.name: xlora_dropout_p
parameters.description: Dropout between its hidden layers; unused at depth one.

parameters.name: use_trainable_adapters
parameters.description: Train the experts too.

parameters.name: softmax_temperature
parameters.description: Divides the logits before the softmax; lower is sharper.

parameters.name: top_k_lora
parameters.description: Keep only this many experts per token (the rest weigh zero).

parameters.name: scaling_pass_value
parameters.description: The weight every expert has in the scalings pass; `0` makes that pass the base model.

parameters.name: global_scaling_weight
parameters.description: A factor on every expert's update.

raises.description: A field holds a value of the wrong type.
A count is not positive, or `top_k_lora` is below one.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import XLoraConfig
>>> config = XLoraConfig(hidden_size=64, adapters={"a": "/tmp/a", "b": "/tmp/b"}, xlora_depth=2)
>>> config.peft_type, sorted(config.adapters)
(<PeftType.XLORA: 'XLORA'>, ['a', 'b'])
>>> XLoraConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config
True

members.summary: A model whose LoRA experts are weighed per token by a classifier on its hidden states.
members.extended:
Construction loads the LoRA adapters `config.adapters` names (as `"0"`, `"1"`, ... through
the multi-adapter API, all active together), switches their layers to the base module and
hooks each to add the experts' updates, scaled.  A call then runs twice: a *scalings pass*,
without gradients, on the model with every expert held at `scaling_pass_value`, whose final
hidden states the classifier (`internal_xlora_classifier`) turns into one weight per expert
and token; and the real pass, in which each adapted layer adds
$g\sum_k u_k(s_k\odot x)$.  The classifier is the only thing that trains (the experts as
well with `use_trainable_adapters`), and the only thing the adapter file holds.

The scalings need the whole sequence at every step: generate with `use_cache=False`.  Layers
of the experts must be `nn.Linear` LoRA layers, without DoRA.  Nothing merges.  The model
keeps one X-LoRA adapter.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The base model; its trunk (`base_model_prefix`) should return `last_hidden_state`.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The experts and the classifier.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the X-LoRA adapter (the experts keep their own names).

parameters.name: device
parameters.description:
The reference loads the experts onto this device.  They load onto the model's own;
anything but `None` raises `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: ephemeral_gpu_offload
parameters.description: Not implemented: `True` raises `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: autocast_adapter_dtype
parameters.description: Always the case here; `False` raises `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
Accepted for the reference's signature (it forwards them to its loader); any key
raises `NotImplementedError`.

raises.description:
The model already holds adapters, `config.adapters` is empty or names a directory
that holds no LoRA adapter, an expert uses DoRA, or the model gives no hidden size.
An expert adapts a layer that is not an `nn.Linear`.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> import tempfile
>>> from lucid.models import create_model
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, XLoraConfig, XLoraModel, get_peft_model
>>> arch = dict(vocab_size=32, hidden_size=16, num_hidden_layers=2, num_attention_heads=2,
...             intermediate_size=32, max_position_embeddings=16)
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     for name in ("a", "b"):
...         get_peft_model(create_model("gpt2_small_lm", **arch),
...                        LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["c_attn"])).save_pretrained(f"{d}/{name}")
...     lm = create_model("gpt2_small_lm", **arch)
...     xlora = XLoraModel(lm, XLoraConfig(adapters={"a": f"{d}/a", "b": f"{d}/b"}), "default")
...     out = xlora(lucid.randint(0, 32, (1, 5)))
>>> out.logits.shape, xlora.get_latest_scalings().shape   # (batch, tokens, layers, experts)
((1, 5, 32), (1, 5, 2, 2))

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.xlora` — X-LoRA: a mixture of LoRA experts weighed per token by a learned classifier.
extended:
X-LoRA (Buehler & Buehler, 2024, [arXiv:2402.07148](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07148)) starts from several LoRA adapters trained on
different tasks and learns only how to combine them.  A scalings pass runs the model with the
experts held at a fixed weight; a small classifier on its final hidden states then predicts, for
every token (and, if asked, every adapted layer), one weight per expert; the real pass adds each
expert's low-rank update on the input scaled by its weight, optionally keeping only the top-k.
Pick it to specialise a model on a mix of skills without choosing one expert up front, and to
train a few thousand classifier parameters rather than the experts.

The experts are loaded by name through the multi-adapter API (`XLoraModel.lora_model`), the
model is called as usual, and the adapter file holds the classifier alone
(`internal_xlora_classifier.*`) — the experts stay where they were saved, named by
`XLoraConfig.adapters`.  The weights come from the whole sequence, so generate with
`use_cache=False`; nothing merges.  `XLoraConfig` and `XLoraModel` are here and exported from
`lucid.peft`; `XLoraClassifier` is the classifier.  Importing the package registers the method
under `PeftType.XLORA`.
citation: Buehler, Eric L., and Markus J. Buehler. "X-LoRA: Mixture of Low-Rank Adapter Experts, a Flexible Framework for Large Language Models with Applications in Protein Mechanics and Molecular Design." [arXiv:2402.07148](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07148), 2024.
theory:
X-LoRA (Buehler & Buehler, 2024, [arXiv:2402.07148](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07148)) keeps several trained LoRA adapters (the
experts) and a small classifier on the base model's final hidden states that scales each
expert per token: a scalings pass computes the hidden states with the experts held at a
fixed value, the classifier turns them into one weight per expert (per adapted layer if
`layerwise_scalings`), and the real pass adds each expert's update with its weight.  Only the
classifier trains unless `use_trainable_adapters`.
